posts.title: Leapmotor posts record September deliveries, tops 100,000 for third straight month
posts.summary:
Leapmotor delivered 105,656 vehicles in September, bringing third-quarter deliveries to a record 310,052.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Leapmotor delivered a record 105,656 vehicles in September, maintaining a monthly volume above 100,000 for the third straight month.
Third-quarter deliveries reached 310,052, bringing the year-to-date total to 666,539, which already surpasses the company's full-year 2025 performance.
To reach its 1,000,000-unit annual target, Leapmotor must deliver an average of 111,154 vehicles per month in the fourth quarter.
International expansion continues via the Leapmotor International joint venture with Stellantis, with exports exceeding 27,000 vehicles in September.

posts.title: Nio delivers 37,408 vehicles in September, meets Q3 guidance
posts.summary:
Deliveries by the Nio brand rose 55.29% year-on-year in September, Firefly set a monthly record and Onvo posted a second consecutive year-on-year decline.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Nio Inc delivered 37,408 vehicles in September, successfully meeting its third-quarter guidance range of 108,000 to 111,000 units.
Performance diverged across brands: the Nio brand grew 55.29% year-on-year, while the Onvo brand experienced its second consecutive month of year-on-year decline.
The Firefly brand emerged as a key growth driver, delivering a record 7,327 vehicles and accounting for the majority of the company's month-on-month delivery increase.

posts.title: Mitigating Threats With Pre-Silicon Security Verification
posts.summary:
The types of threats that must be mitigated and a process to verify that designs are secure in real-world deployment.
The post Mitigating Threats With Pre-Silicon Security Verification appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Security verification must now occur at the pre-silicon stage to prevent hardware-level vulnerabilities that could lead to system compromise or data theft.
Modern threats extend beyond software-based attacks, requiring designers to account for malicious actors attempting to manipulate hardware behavior directly.
The integration of security into the design flow is becoming as critical as functional safety, particularly for high-stakes applications like autonomous vehicles and industrial control.

posts.title: Why LLMs Are The Best Thing To Happen To Chip Design
posts.summary:
Moving beyond RTL to a new representation that allows engineers to express intent more intuitively.
The post Why LLMs Are The Best Thing To Happen To Chip Design appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The pursuit of AGI is driving a surge in custom silicon development, as major tech companies seek to optimize infrastructure for large-scale model training.
Chip design complexity has reached a point where traditional manual methods are insufficient, necessitating new AI-driven representations to express engineering intent.
Verification has emerged as the primary bottleneck in the chip design cycle, consuming the majority of engineering effort in modern ASIC development.

posts.title: Open Security Foundations Are Only The Beginning: Deploying Caliptra Hardware in Production
posts.summary:
Roots of trust are beginning to assume a broader role as platform security orchestrators.
The post Open Security Foundations Are Only The Beginning: Deploying Caliptra Hardware in Production appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The industry is increasingly adopting open-source silicon Roots of Trust like Caliptra to standardize security across heterogeneous data center hardware.
As data center architectures become more complex, establishing consistent trust across components from multiple suppliers has become a critical operational challenge.
Open-source security architectures provide the transparency required for cloud providers to verify device identity and code integrity throughout the hardware lifecycle.
